item.description: • Profile Tabs' rail shows its profiles again, instead of a blank strip at the window's left.

• Settings > Scheduled can stop a scheduled prompt's run while it works, or show its chat.
  • Removing a scheduled prompt in Settings > Scheduled now also stops its run in progress.
  • Tab layout, the tab sidebar's width and collapsed state, and tab unloading are the same in every profile.
  • Settings in Settings > Agent and Settings > Jev now apply to every profile.
  • Custom providers in Settings > Providers and skills in Settings > Skills are shared by every profile.
  • Existing settings come from the default profile, and skills from all profiles are merged into one library.
  • Switching profiles no longer shows the last profile's tabs through the sidebar while its agent works.

• Extensions see Tiller's tabs and windows, so chrome.tabs.query finds the current tab.
  • Extension popups that act on the current tab, such as a page clipper's, now find it.
  • Extensions can open, select and close Tiller tabs, so 1Password's sign-in tab can finish.
  • 1Password unlocks with its Mac app and shows your items, instead of an endless sign-in page.
  • Extensions that talk to a Mac app, such as 1Password, can now connect to it, once the app trusts Tiller.

• Fix a crash when an extension opens a tab as it's added or as Tiller starts.
  • Pages an extension opens, such as its options or welcome page, open in a Tiller tab, not a Chromium window.
  • Extensions added from the Chrome Web Store join Settings > Extensions and every profile at the next launch.

• The agent panel's message field is restyled after Codex's: a rounder card with more room around the text, whose edge firms up under the mouse and with focus instead of glowing in the accent, and a send button in the text's color. The thinking effort has a button of its own next to the model, which opens just the efforts, and the hint mentions / for skills. The field eases taller and shorter as lines come and go, the send arrow lifts away as a message goes and turns into the stop square while the agent works, and images dragged over the field show a Drop images to attach hint. Reduce Motion turns the motion off.
  • A microphone button beside the send button starts dictation into the agent panel's message field. While the agent works, a short arc circles inside the stop button. The model and effort names, the tools button's tint and the field's hint fade into their new values, and the effort button fades in for a model that has efforts. Reduce Motion turns the motion off.
  • A /name at the start of the agent panel's message field that calls a skill shows as a token, in the accent on a soft plate. The skill list rises in from the field and shows what was typed in the accent in each name, and a message taller than the field fades out at the edge with more text beyond it.
  • Type @ in the agent panel's message field to mention another open tab: pick one from the list, which shows each tab's icon and address, and its address goes in the message.
  • A small ring before the microphone button shows how much of the model's context window the chat takes, once the agent reports it, turning orange from 80% and red from 95%. Its tooltip gives the numbers.

• Closing the last tab keeps the window and profile open on the configured new tab page. The closed page can still be reopened with Cmd+Shift+T; closing a window or profile, or quitting Tiller, works as before.
  • Apps that list browsers, such as link pickers, now include Tiller, and a web page handed off from another device opens in Tiller.
  • A file path typed or pasted in the address bar, such as /Users/me/page.html or ~/page.html, opens the file instead of searching for it.
  • Small things ease in instead of popping: the zoom and saved-password badges in the address bar, a tab's recording dot, the agent's status and busy dots, a finished tool call's check, new messages and the Thinking row in a chat, pasted images in the message field, a chat's suggestions, a new download, and a new tab in the sidebar. The page-load bar and the agent button's dot, which were meant to fade, now do. Copy and a finished download's Show in Finder give a small pop. The caret in the address bar and the message field takes the theme's accent. Reduce Motion turns all of it off.
  • In dark mode the address bar's suggestions are no longer a light grey over a dark page: the list takes the theme's own color, with the page showing through a little.
  • The tab sidebar keeps the width it was given when Tiller opens and when it is collapsed and expanded, rather than growing to its widest. Collapsing or expanding it fades its rows into their new shape.
  • Less work while a chat streams and scrolls: the agent's reasoning updates the Thinking row a few times a second rather than on every word, a chat in the background no longer lays itself out, icons and hover colors are made once and reused, and dragging the sidebar's edge saves its width when the drag stops. Typing in the address bar looks through the open tabs once per edit rather than on every key, and / in the message field reads your skill folders in the background after the first time.
  • The find bar and the camera and microphone bar drop into place as they fade in, a closed tab fades out while the others close up, and each time the start page comes up its tiles and closed tabs come in one after another.
  • On a narrow page the start page takes fewer columns instead of cutting its tiles and closed tabs off at the left, and a single site's tile sits centered under its heading.
  • The find bar's field is less see-through, so the page's own text no longer shows through it.
  • On a narrow page the find bar and the camera and microphone bar narrow to fit, instead of widening the page and pushing the agent panel aside. At the narrowest the camera bar's buttons take a smaller size.
  • In dark mode the address bar keeps a faint edge at rest, so it still shows where to type when the tabs are along the top.
  • With only one or a few frequently visited sites, the start page's tiles and their heading sit centered on the page again, rather than off to the left with the heading out of line with the tile.
  • Switching to another chat in the agent panel, opening one from history or closing a chat's tab fades the chat that takes the panel in rather than cutting to it; the chat tabs and the message field stay still.
  • The tip beside a profile in the profile rail fades in and out instead of popping, and moving from one profile to the next just changes it.
  • Timers that tick each second while an agent works, and the check for tabs to unload, give the system leeway to batch their wakeups. Agent events that arrive together lay out the chat once rather than once each.

• On the start page, recently closed tabs with long titles line up with the others again.
  • The tiller command-line tool does what Tiller's menus and Settings do. tiller profile lists, opens, creates, renames, colors, labels, moves, closes and deletes profiles, and --profile opens a closed profile, or starts Tiller, before it acts. New commands go back and forward, reload, stop, find text, zoom, save a PDF, duplicate, move and reopen tabs, close other tabs, and show the page's source or Developer Tools. tiller history, downloads, settings, sites, passwords, extensions and import chrome manage those, tiller agent send sends a message to an agent and prints its answer, tiller skills and tiller schedules manage the skill library and scheduled prompts, and tiller show brings up the agent panel, downloads, the find bar or a Settings pane. tiller <area> --help lists an area's commands.
  • An agent's chat that runs tiller can still use the browser, history search, skills and schedules, but Tiller refuses its requests to manage profiles, settings, logins, extensions and the rest.
  • Agents get six more browser tools: back, forward, reload, finding text in the page, zoom and history search.

• Tiller now passes as Chrome to sites that check the browser, such as sign-in pages that said they couldn't verify it. Its user agent no longer adds Tiller's name, and its client hints name Google Chrome as Chrome's do, in every page, frame and worker. A popup's first page may load twice for it.
  • The address bar works more like Chrome's. Typing completes the address of a page you've typed or visited before right in the bar, and the list under it adds the search engine's suggestions, which Settings > General can turn off, and open tabs to switch to. Up and Down put each row in the bar and wrap round, Tab moves through the list too, Shift+Delete or a row's cross removes a page from history, and Ctrl+Return adds www. and .com. Pages you typed rank higher. Clicking the bar, Cmd+L or Down lists recent pages and a link you copied.
  • At rest the address bar leaves out https://, www. and a lone trailing slash, which right-click > Always Show Full URLs keeps. Http pages say "Not Secure", and the icon before the address opens the site's information with its camera and microphone permissions. The right-click menu has Paste and Go, and a drag in the bar selects part of the address.
  • On the start page, a recently closed tab with a long address shows its title again; the address is cut short instead of the title.
  • Profile Tabs: View > Profile Tabs, or Settings > Profiles, puts every open profile in one window, with a rail on its left to switch between them. Each square shows two letters of the profile's name, tinted in the profile's color, the one shown ringed and marked by a pill in its color along the rail's edge. Its tip gives the name, the keys that show it, the profile's tab count and the page in front. The dashed + opens another profile, a drag reorders them, a link dropped on a square opens in that profile, right-click renames one, picks its color, gives it a label of one or two characters, an emoji too, in place of its initials, or closes it, and with many profiles the rail scrolls. Each profile keeps its own toolbar, tabs and agent panel, and one out of sight keeps running, with a dot that pulses while its agent works and stays once it finishes, until the profile shows. Closing the window closes every profile, and they all open again at the next launch. Turning it on gathers the windows into one, and off parts them again.
  • Each profile has a color, which shows as its avatar in the Profiles menu and beside its name in the toolbar. Profiles without a color of their own pass over the colors others picked, so two don't share one until there are more than eight.
  • Window > Show Next Profile (Ctrl+Cmd+]) and Show Previous Profile (Ctrl+Cmd+[), and Ctrl+Cmd+1 to Ctrl+Cmd+9, go to another open profile.
  • The cross beside a download in the Downloads list cancels it again, and downloads from different profiles no longer get mixed up.

• Themes: Settings > General > Theme gives Tiller Claude's colors, Anthropic's ivory or warm near-black with Claude's orange, or Qoder's Forest greens, each light or dark as the appearance is. The window, sidebar, toolbar, agent panel and start page take the theme's colors and accent; Tiller's own theme keeps the system's look.

• The agent's message field is redesigned: the text spans the field's full width above a row of controls, with the add button, the chat's model by name, the tools and a new round send button that turns into a stop button while a turn runs. The model and tools menus open from the field, above it, and while the agent works the hint says what you write is queued. The new tab button sits right after the tab numbers.
  • Sending a message to the agent no longer asks for the login keychain password to check whether run_task's keys are set; Tiller reads a key only when it uses one, once per launch. Development builds keep their provider and Jev keys apart from the installed Tiller's.
  • While Jev works on a page, the page shows the step it is on, the time so far and a Stop button, and rings each field and button before it acts on it. The agent's chat shows the step under the task, and once it ends whether it got there, with its step count and time, or why it stopped.
  • Settings > Jev says whether agents get run_task and what is missing, links to where keys come from, and Check Keys tries both keys and shows how long each model took to answer.
  • Agents hand getting somewhere or setting something up on a page, such as opening a story's comments, filling a search form or setting filters, to TypeSafe's Jev with the new run_task tool, or tiller run "<goal>": Jev picks each click, field and option in a few hundred milliseconds instead of a turn per step, and a small text model writes what goes in the fields. Agents get the tool once a TypeSafe key is added in Settings > Jev.
  • Clicks that don't load a page return in about a quarter of a second instead of a second, and click, type and the new select take read: true to return the page after acting, saving the agent a step.
  • read_page refs stay the same while an element stays on the page and are no longer written into the page, and acting on one whose element has changed fails instead of clicking the wrong thing. It also lists fields by their labels, with their values, checked and expanded state and a dropdown's options, leaves out hidden controls, and takes viewport to list only what is on screen.
  • The new select tool, and tiller choose, pick a dropdown's option. type clicks the field before typing, so fields that open suggestions or a search box of their own on a click get the text.
  • The agent's message field remembers what you sent: Up on its first line brings back earlier messages from any chat, Down goes forward again, and Ctrl+R searches them. The paperclip is now a plus button whose menu adds images or opens the search.
  • When Tiller quits unexpectedly right after opening, the next launch starts without extensions and says so, with a link to Extensions settings. An extension that opens a tab as Tiller starts could otherwise crash it at every launch, before it could be switched off.
  • While the agent works through a run of steps, the chat shows only its newest step under the step count instead of a growing list; click the count to see them all. A running script or command gets lines of its own instead of wrapping word by word, a finished step keeps one line, and hovering a step shows its whole input.

• window.open without a size returns the new tab's window, so a page can open a blank tab and send it somewhere afterwards.
  • With no recently closed tabs below them, the start page's tiles sit centered instead of at the left of an empty row.
  • A page fades in from under the start page, and from the cover a new tab shows in dark mode, instead of cutting in. In dark mode a new page shows as soon as it has nearly loaded, and pages from Back and Forward show sooner.
  • Address suggestions and extension popups fade in and out. Opening a suggestion still closes the list at once.
  • The tab sidebar can no longer be dragged so narrow that tabs lose their titles while it is still expanded.
  • Tooltips on tabs, the new-tab row, suggestions and downloads no longer stop showing after the mouse has moved over them.
  • Middle-clicking closes a tab only when the click both starts and ends on that tab.
  • The address bar, favicons, the downloads button and window resizing do less repeated work.
  • Resizing the window or the agent panel only rewraps the chat messages in view, and catches up on the rest when the drag ends. A code block streaming in measures only its new lines, and opening a saved chat no longer starts and stops a spinner for each step.
  • In agents' answers, nested lists indent one level per level however many spaces they use, a list item's wrapped lines line up with its text, and numbered and bulleted items' text starts at the same place. Task lists show checkboxes instead of brackets, with finished tasks dimmed, and links in quotes keep their color.
  • Tables have the same corners as code blocks, the empty chat's suggestions line up their text, and an error's Try Again button matches the panel's other buttons.
  • In Settings → General, "Unload after" and "Custom search URL" dim their labels too when the setting they depend on is off, and the note under the search URL says to pick Custom to use it.
  • Agent tool results, stderr from an agent's CLI, replies to the tiller tool and download progress do less work on the main thread.
  • Start page tiles no longer rebuild and fade in again when a page title or icon changes; a tile updates in place. Very small site icons are no longer stretched to full size, and the background grain is drawn at full resolution on Retina screens.
  • Clear History also removes the cleared pages from the history file itself, rather than leaving them in its journal and free space.
  • Saving open tabs no longer writes on the main thread after every tab change, and the session file is private from the moment it is written. Saved passwords load in the background as a profile opens.
  • Opening another tab of a site no longer rewrites its icon to history, and history queries reuse their prepared statements.
  • Back and forward mouse side buttons work with Logi Options+ too, which sends swipe gestures instead of standard mouse button events on macOS.

• The agent chat fades out under its header and above the message field as it scrolls, instead of cutting a line in half at the edge.
  • The start page's tiles line up from the left when there are fewer than four, rather than spreading out with gaps between them.
  • Address suggestions line up their icons and titles with the address field's icon and text.
  • Small polish: Copy and download buttons light up under the mouse, a tab's close button and the skill picker fade in, steps fold away with a fade when a turn ends, queued messages show a press, the find bar's close button has a round plate, chat history dates are easier to read, and Remote debugging moves to the end of Settings → General.
  • Chats in background tabs or a hidden panel no longer redraw streamed text 20 times a second; they catch up when shown.
  • Scrolling a long tab sidebar only moves the tabs in view, and resizing the window lays out the toolbar once, when the drag ends.
  • The Downloads list no longer updates while closed, and the first message to an agent no longer freezes the window while a login shell looks for its command.
  • Importing a long Chrome history no longer holds up the address bar's suggestions and the start page until it finishes.

• Background tabs left unused for 30 minutes unload to free their memory, and sooner when the Mac runs low on memory. An unloaded tab keeps its place, shows a dimmed title and icon, and loads again when selected. Tabs playing media, using the camera or microphone, or asking before you leave stay loaded. Settings → General turns it off or sets the delay.
  • Agents and the tiller tool no longer load every tab restored at launch. They load only the tab they act on, and list_tabs says whether each tab is loaded. Tab ids stay the same while a tab is unloaded.
  • Fixed a crash in the agent chat with a mouse attached, when a conversation grew to about one screen tall.
  • Back and forward mouse side buttons now navigate the selected tab, including Logitech mice with standard button assignments.
